Ticket.title: Ticket
Ticket.description: Represents a maintenance or facility ticket.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Ticket entity.

description.description: Detailed explanation of the ticket request.

requestedCompletionDate.description: The date by which the ticket completion is requested.

location.description: The location associated with the ticket (e.g., room number, building).

status.description: The current status of the ticket (e.g., Not Started, In Progress, Pending Review, Completed).

assignedToUserId.description: Reference to User. User to whom the ticket is assigned. (Relationship: User 1:N Ticket)

createdDate.description: The date and time when the ticket was created.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a category for organizing tasks.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

parentCategoryId.description: Reference to Parent Category. The ID of the parent category, if any. (Relationship: Category 1:N Category)

id.description: Unique identifier for the RecurringTask entity.

categoryId.description: Reference to Category. The category associated with the recurring task. (Relationship: Category 1:N RecurringTask)

scheduleType.description: The type of schedule (e.g., Daily, Weekly, Monthly).

scheduleDetails.description: Details of when the task is scheduled. This could be a JSON string with the details of how often to create the ticket.

assignedToUserId.description: Reference to User. The user to whom the recurring task is assigned. (Relationship: User 1:N RecurringTask)

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

role.description: The role of the user (e.g., Viewer, Staff, Admin).

email.description: The email address of the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Setting entity.

value.description: The value of the setting. Store as a string.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support a ticket-based task management system (FacilityFlow) with features like ticket creation, management, user roles, category management, recurring task scheduling, settings configuration, and a user management interface. The structure prioritizes authorization independence via denormalization, structural segregation for a homogeneous security posture, and access modeling for standardization and consistency.

**Authorization Independence:** User roles are stored within the user document itself. This eliminates the need for complex `get()` calls in security rules, supporting atomic operations and improving debuggability.

**Structural Segregation:** Each collection is designed to hold documents with similar access control requirements. For example, user-specific data (like assigned tickets and recurring tasks) are stored under the `/users/{userId}` path, while global categories and settings reside in separate collections.

**QAPs Support:**
*   **List Operations:** Segregation of data into collections with homogeneous security postures ensures secure list operations. Rules can be applied at the collection level to control access based on user roles or ownership.
*   **Category and Settings:** Global categories and settings are stored in dedicated collections (`/categories`, `/settings`), allowing for easy management and secure access control based on user roles (e.g., only admins can modify categories and settings).
*   **User Roles:** Roles are stored on the User document in `/users/{userId}` and are secure based on path-based ownership.
